To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a glnB mutation alters the expression of the glnBA and glnll genes, but not that of glnA and the ntrBC genes.

a glnB mutation in Rhizobium leads to a loss of Ntr regulation of glnA, glnII and glnBA, and to a loss of the ability to use nitrate as a nitrogen source, but that Ntr regulation of ntrC is unaffected.
the P11 protein plays a negative role, in the absence of the PII protein, in the ability of the NtrC protein to activate transcription from the ntrBC and glnA promoters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of nitrogen metabolism in the glnBA operon.
the regulation of nitrogen assimilation in the rhizobia and the role played by the PII protein.
the role of the glnB‐P11 protein in nitrogen regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
glnB mutants are altered in the regulation of nitrogen metabolism.
the glnA gene product is the only enzyme involved in nitrogen assimilation in Rhizobium, while the P11 protein has a regulatory role in the expression of the genes involved in nitrogen metabolism.
glnB is involved in nitrogen metabolism regulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the P11 protein acts as a repressor for the glnA and the ntrBC genes, and as an activator for glnBA and glnll.
the P11 protein plays a positive role in nitrate utilization and that the NtrC protein is a repressor for nitrate utilization.
glnB mutants of R. leguminosarumsynthesize the Ntr system proteins but do not respond to nitrogen limitation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the P11 protein is involved in the regulation of nitrogen metabolism, but the mechanism of action of the P11 protein remains to be elucidated.

the GlnB protein, which is known to be a key component of a two‐component regulatory system (NtrBC) involved in the regulation of nitrogen metabolism in Rhizobium, is also involved in nitrate utilization.
the glnBA gene cluster is not a single operon, and glnB and glnA can be regulated independently.
